protocol.title: Node lesson 2 — Bindings & modifiers
protocol.summary: A guided build: wire a constant into an input's max (a binding), then gate the dose onto the document through a 📊 Cards node — settings wires and display wires in one lesson.

chips.text: you build it — nothing is pre-made

children.body: How this lesson works. The guided tour is running in the ⬡ Nodes view. Lesson 1 wired variables into an equation; here a wire does something different — it drives a node's setting. That kind of wire is called a binding, and you'll build two.

Build 1: a Constant named upper_cap (value 100) wired into the max setting of a dose slider. Once built, drag upper_cap's value up or down — the dose slider's maximum moves with it. A binding keeps two settings in lock-step.

How you'll make it: on a node, click “+ add modifier” at the bottom. That menu lists everything a node can accept — for an Input it offers “Drive min / max / step / default from a variable…”. Choosing one arms that setting's left dot (it pulses); then you click the variable's right dot to complete the wire. Every binding is discoverable through this menu.

Build 2: a display gate. A 📊 Cards node decides what the document shows — wire dose into it and the chosen dose renders as a live result card, read-only. Nothing displays by itself: ungated variables still compute, they just aren't offered to the page. (Card variables are automatically available to the editor's 🔗 reference picker too; a separate 🔗 References node offers values inline without a card.)

The binding roles, in plain terms. math — the variable is usable by name inside an Equation (or a Code node) formula. param — the variable's live value overrides one numeric setting on the target node (min, max, step, default, decimals). structural — a set feeds a List, changing what items exist rather than any single number. display — the variable is offered to the document: as a result card (📊 Cards) or as an inline reference (🔗 References). none — legacy wires with no effect; delete them.

Live check (after the build): the dose input currently reads [!var:dose], and the same value sits on the document as a gated card. Raise upper_cap, then push dose past its old ceiling to prove the binding really moved the max — typed values above the cap snap back, and lowering the cap pulls a saved dose down with it.

You now know three wire kinds: feeding a formula (math), driving a setting (param), and gating a value onto the document (display). Lesson 3 builds the fourth — structural feeds — turning sets of options into an experiment list laid out on plates.
